options: Current / A
The current measured
Current (amperes) / A

answer: Current / A

note: Selecting the largest of three temperature rises is a simple comparison, not L4. Heat inference also needs comparable mass and thermal conditions.
question: Equal volumes of three acids are neutralised by the same alkali. The temperature rises by 5.2, 6.8 and 4.1 °C. Which released the most heat?
options: The one that rose by 5.2 °C
They all released the same heat
The one that rose by 4.1 °C
The one that rose by 6.8 °C
answer: The one that rose by 6.8 °C

note: The credible option is compared with choosing the fastest-loading or prettiest website. This allows common-sense elimination without chemistry reasoning.
question: Two websites give different values for the pH of rainwater. What is the best next step?
options: Use the value from the page that loaded fastest
Look for a third, independent source and compare
Write both down and let the reader pick one
Take the value that appears on the prettier page
answer: Look for a third, independent source and compare

note: Unsupported website claim: useful scientific literacy, but weak alternatives make L4 excessive. Ask pupils to evaluate competing evidence.
question: A claim on a website has no author, no date and no references. How should it be treated?
options: As true because it is written down
As unsupported until it is checked
As proved because a website printed it
As false because there is no author
answer: As unsupported until it is checked

note: Asks for the function of the oviduct: direct biological knowledge, labelled Hard. The topic is legitimate; its cognitive demand is mislabelled.
question: What is the function of the oviduct?
options: It filters waste products out of the blood
It carries the egg from the ovary towards the uterus
It produces the female sex cells each month
It is where the baby develops before birth
answer: It carries the egg from the ovary towards the uterus

question: Choisis la forme correcte : « Il a voulu .......... la porte. »
options: fermait
fermé
fermant
fermer

note: Selecting a structure for a literary response does not assess constructing and supporting that response.
question: Une question longue sur une œuvre demande une réponse développée. Quelle structure convient ?
options: Une opinion personnelle sans aucune référence au texte
La liste de tous les personnages de l’œuvre étudiée
Une idée, un exemple tiré de l’œuvre, une conclusion
Un résumé complet de l’intrigue de l’œuvre entière
answer: Une idée, un exemple tiré de l’œuvre, une conclusion

note: Choosing advice about lengthening writing is not producing 50–75 words; distractors include copying and repetition.
question: Comment augmenter un texte de 40 mots à 50 mots sans hors-sujet ?
options: Ajouter une introduction hors-sujet
Développer davantage les points imposés en ajoutant des détails, des exemples ou des précisions
Copier une partie du sujet
Répéter les mêmes phrases
answer: Développer davantage les points imposés en ajoutant des détails, des exemples ou des précisions

note: Simple figurative meaning is contrasted with literal chairs making sounds. L4 overstates the reasoning elicited.
question: Explain the line: "The empty chair at the table spoke louder than any words."
options: Chairs can literally make sounds
The absence of someone was felt more powerfully than speech
No one sat down for the meal
The family argued very loudly at dinner
answer: The absence of someone was felt more powerfully than speech

note: Recognising the only developed, evidence-bearing response does not demonstrate independent literary analysis.
question: Which response about an author's purpose is most convincing?
options: "The author wants to challenge complacency: the statistic 'one in four' appears three times, hammering the scale of the problem"
"The author is trying to persuade the reader"
"The author wants to make the reader think"
"The author has a clear purpose in this text"
answer: "The author wants to challenge complacency: the statistic 'one in four' appears three times, hammering the scale of the problem"

note: Selecting ability to pay school fees is a short causal recognition item, not a developed explanation at Hard level.
question: Before free secondary education, what mainly decided whether a child continued to secondary school?
options: Whether the family could pay the fees
The child's age in years
The child's district of birth
The size of the school building
answer: Whether the family could pay the fees

note: Distractors claiming Mauritius has no meteorological service or cyclones only form above small islands make elimination too easy.
question: Why are cyclones particularly damaging to small island nations like Mauritius?
options: A small island has no large land mass to weaken a cyclone before it reaches settled areas
Mauritius lacks a meteorological service capable of tracking cyclones
Cyclones only ever form directly above small islands in the Indian Ocean
Small islands always produce stronger cyclones than large countries
answer: A small island has no large land mass to weaken a cyclone before it reaches settled areas

note: The stem rules out copper hydroxide because it is insoluble, but insoluble bases can be used with acid to prepare salts. Correct this misleading premise before judging difficulty.
question: A student wishes to prepare a pure dry sample of copper sulfate by neutralisation. She cannot use copper hydroxide because it is insoluble. What method should she use?
options: Add excess copper metal to dilute sulfuric acid, filter, then crystallise
Electrolyse copper sulfate solution and collect the salt from the electrodes
Add sodium hydroxide to copper sulfate solution and filter the copper sulfate that precipitates
Add excess copper oxide (a base) to warm dilute sulfuric acid, filter off the excess solid, then crystallise the filtrate
answer: Add excess copper oxide (a base) to warm dilute sulfuric acid, filter off the excess solid, then crystallise the filtrate

note: Two options both say excess reactant contaminates the salt. A single-answer MCQ should not offer two equivalent correct statements.
question: Why is excess acid (or excess base) a problem in the preparation of a pure salt by neutralisation?
options: Excess acid (or excess base) will contaminate the final salt product and make it impure
Excess reactant reacts with the salt product and destroys it
Excess reactant will contaminate the final salt product and make it impure
Excess reactant makes the solution too concentrated to crystallise
answer: Excess acid (or excess base) will contaminate the final salt product and make it impure

note: The question says changes since the last FULL backup but keys incremental; this wording describes differential backup. Review and correct the distinction.
question: Which backup method copies only the files that have changed since the last full backup?
options: Mirror backup
Manual backup
Full backup
Incremental backup
answer: Incremental backup

question: A rectangle has the same area and a length of 33 cm. Find its width. (answer in cm)

note: Passive transformation in the pluperfect demands real grammatical discrimination, although producing it would test more than choosing it.
question: Mets à la voix passive (plus-que-parfait) : « Le médecin avait examiné la patiente. »
options: La patiente était examinée par le médecin.
La patiente avait été examinée du médecin.
La patiente a été examinée par le médecin.
La patiente avait été examinée par le médecin.
answer: La patiente avait été examinée par le médecin.

note: Distinguishing correlation from sole causation is relevant scientific reasoning. Improve distractor balance rather than remove the outcome.
question: A graph shows cardiovascular death rates falling steadily over 20 years in a country that introduced a national anti-smoking campaign in the same period. What is the most reasonable interpretation?
options: The decline in deaths has nothing to do with the campaign and is due entirely to genetics
The anti-smoking campaign is the sole proven cause of every reduction in deaths
Reduced smoking may have contributed to the fall, though other factors may also be involved
Cardiovascular death rates always decrease over time regardless of any interventions
answer: Reduced smoking may have contributed to the fall, though other factors may also be involved
